title: Crossword dictionary
prompt:
Build a crossword helper whose add(word) stores a word and find(pattern) reports whether some stored word matches the pattern, where '.' stands for any one letter.

- Implement the WordBook class; runWordBook / run_word_book (already written) replays ops, a list like [["add", "cat"], ["find", "c.t"]], and returns one output per op: null (None) for add, a boolean for find.
- A match must have the same length as the pattern. Words are lowercase a-z; patterns are lowercase a-z and '.'; both are 1 to 20 characters.
- Up to 10,000 ops; each pattern contains at most 3 dots.
hints: Scanning every stored word for each find is slow when there are many words. How can words with a common beginning share work?
Store words in a trie with an end-of-word flag. A literal letter follows one edge; a '.' must try every child.
Search with a stack (or recursion) of (node, index) pairs. When index reaches the pattern length, succeed if the node ends a word; otherwise keep exploring the remaining branches.

solution.explanation: A trie lets a lookup follow one edge per literal letter, independent of how many words are stored. A '.' fans out to every child at that depth, and the search succeeds only at a node that marks the end of a word, which enforces equal length.

complexity.time: O(L) per add; O(26^d * L) per find
complexity.notes: L is the word or pattern length and d the number of dots; a pattern without dots is O(L). In practice the fan-out is limited to children that actually exist.

followUps: Support '*' meaning any sequence of letters (including none). How does the search change?
